raw_response:
The silver_transactions step sets txn_date = CAST(ingest_ts AS DATE). Ingest happens at 02:00 the day after the transaction, so txn_date is shifted one day from the date of txn_ts. This came from the 2026-01-16 refactor (DE-398). The alert counts 4600 mismatches, which equals all POSTED rows, so every row is affected. The fix is to derive txn_date from txn_ts. Checks on the evidence: - Transaction timestamps run 06:00–22:59, so ingest at 02:00 the next day always shifts the date. There is no ambiguity. - The alert wording says txn_date should equal the date of txn_ts. - Other columns are unchanged, and gold tables rebuild from silver. The gold steps depend on silver_transactions, so they are rerun in the pipeline. Overriding only silver is enough, since the gold steps run after it. Could txn_date be intended as the ingest date? The monitor defines consistency as txn_date matching txn_ts, and the column name says transaction date. The change note says the date derivation was refactored, which points to this as the regression.
{"diagnosis": "The DE-398 refactor on 2026-01-16 made silver_transactions.txn_date come from ingest_ts (02:00 the next day) instead of txn_ts, shifting every row's date by one day. Deriving txn_date from txn_ts fixes silver and the downstream gold tables.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
